content: True courage is to do without witnesses what one would be capable of doing before all the world.
author: François de La Rochefoucauld
story:
At its core, this reflection cuts through our everyday excuses. Holding onto anger is like clutching a glowing coal with the intent of throwing it at someone else—you are the one who gets burned. Retaliation only ties you tighter to the person who harmed you.

In François de La Rochefoucauld's view, genuine strength is not an abstract theory—it is a lived, daily practice. Forgiveness and composure are not signs of weakness or giving someone a pass. They are acts of fierce self-preservation, cutting the emotional chain that allows another person's bad behavior to ruin your peace of mind.
reflectionPrompt: What hidden motive, insecurity, or fear might be silently driving your recent reactions?

practicalInsight: When someone triggers your temper today, take three slow breaths before responding. Do not give away your power for the sake of a quick comeback.
